test_title: PYST 51: SSC GD Constable 2022 - Quantitative Aptitude(Held On : 01 Feb 2023 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question:
What will be the difference in the compound interest if a sum of Rs. 12,000 is compounded annually and half-yearly at an annual rate of 10% for a period of 2 years?

**Note:** Round off the decimal to the nearest number.
solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 12,000

Rate = 10% per annum

Time = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P × (1 + (r)/(n))ⁿt

Where, P = Principal, r = Rate, t = time(in years)

n = Number of times interest credited per year

**Calculation:**

For interest compounded annually, n = 1

Amount = 12000 × (1 + (10)/(100))²

⇒ Amount = 12000 × (110/100)2

⇒ Amount = 12000 × (11/10)2 = 14520

⇒ CI = 14520 - 12000 = 2520

For interest compounded half yearly, n = 2

Amount = 12000 × (1 + (10)/(2 × 100))2×2

⇒ Amount = 12000 × (1 + (5)/(100))4

⇒ Amount = 12000 × (105/100)4 = 14586.075 ≈ 14586

⇒ CI = 14586 - 12000 = 2586

Difference in CI = 2586 - 2520 = 66 rupees

**∴ The difference in CI is 66 rupees.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Concept:**

Compound Interest difference = P[(1 + r/2n)⁽²ⁿt⁾ - (1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾]

**Calculation:**

⇒ Difference = Rs. 12,000[(1 + 0.1/4)⁽⁴²⁾ - (1 + 0.1/2)⁽²²⁾] = Rs. 66 (approximately)

∴ The difference in CI is 66 rupees.
